recipes.title: Creamy berry vanilla overnight oats
recipes.summary: Oats, chia and Greek yogurt for lasting energy, fiber and protein. Stir it tonight; breakfast is waiting tomorrow.
ingredients: 1/2 cup old-fashioned rolled oats (not instant, which gets too mushy)
1/4 cup plain or vanilla Greek yogurt
1/3 cup fresh or frozen berries (strawberries, blueberries or raspberries)
steps: In a clean 16 oz mason jar or airtight container, stir the milk, yogurt, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth.
Add the oats and chia seeds and stir well, so all the oats are covered and no clumps of chia are left at the bottom.
Gently fold in the berries. Frozen berries thaw overnight and add their juice.
Close the lid and refrigerate for at least 4 hours; overnight (6 to 8 hours) gives the creamiest texture.
In the morning, stir and eat cold straight from the jar, or warm it in the microwave for 45 to 60 seconds.
tips: Warming it up? Spoon it into a microwave-safe bowl first, since not every jar is microwave-safe, and stir before eating.
Top with chopped nuts, a drizzle of peanut butter or extra fruit just before eating. Nuts and peanut butter add common allergens.
Honey is fine for you, but never give honey to a baby under 12 months.
Make 3 or 4 jars at once; they keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Any milk works, including almond or soy milk (these add tree nut or soy). For dairy-free, use a plant milk and a dairy-free yogurt.

recipes.title: Banana oat smoothie
recipes.summary: A thick, filling drink you can sip during a feed.
steps: Add everything to a blender.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
Pour into a cup with a lid and a straw.
tips: Freeze sliced ripe bananas so they're ready to go.
Use fortified soy milk and soy yogurt for a dairy-free version.

recipes.title: Peanut butter banana milkshake
recipes.summary: Creamy, chocolatey and ready in two minutes.
steps: Add everything to a blender.
Blend until thick and smooth.
Drink right away.
tips: Cocoa contains a small amount of caffeine; leave it out if you're keeping caffeine low.

recipes.title: Warm cinnamon vanilla milk
recipes.summary: A cozy, caffeine-free warm drink for night feeds.
steps: Warm the milk in a small pan or the microwave until steaming, not boiling.
Stir in the cinnamon, vanilla and maple syrup.
Pour into a mug with a lid and let it cool to a comfortable temperature.
tips: Use a lidded mug so you can sip safely while holding your baby.
Fortified oat or soy milk work well too.

recipes.title: Creamy oat porridge with peanut butter
recipes.summary: Warm, comforting oats with banana and a swirl of peanut butter.
steps: Add the oats and milk to a small pan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and top with banana, peanut butter and cinnamon.
tips: Microwave option: cook oats and milk in a large bowl for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway.

recipes.title: Veggie egg muffin cups
recipes.summary: Make a dozen on Sunday and reheat all week.
ingredients: 1 cup chopped vegetables (spinach, bell pepper, tomato)
Oil or cooking spray for the pan
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper together.
Divide the vegetables and cheese between the cups, then pour in the egg mixture.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the eggs are firm and fully set in the middle, with no runny egg.
Cool, then refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.
tips: Reheat in the microwave for about 30 seconds until hot all the way through.
Leave out added salt if you'll share these with your baby, and cut a baby's portion into small pieces or thin slices.

recipes.title: Berry yogurt parfait
recipes.summary: Layers of yogurt, fruit and crunchy oats in five minutes.
ingredients: 2 tbsp rolled oats or toasted oats
steps: Spoon half the yogurt into a glass or jar.
Add half the berries and oats, then repeat the layers.
Drizzle with maple syrup if you like.

recipes.title: Avocado toast with egg
recipes.summary: A quick, satisfying breakfast with a fully cooked egg.
steps: Toast the bread.
Fry, scramble or boil the egg until the white and yolk are fully set.
Mash the avocado with lemon and spread on the toast.
Top with the egg and season.

recipes.title: Freezer breakfast burritos
recipes.summary: Wrap, freeze and microwave on busy mornings.
steps: Cook the pepper in the oil until soft.
Add the whisked eggs and scramble until fully cooked. Stir in the beans.
Divide the filling, cheese and salsa between the tortillas and roll up tightly.
Cool, wrap each one in foil or plastic wrap and freeze.
To reheat, unwrap, wrap in a paper towel and microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until hot in the center.
tips: Frozen burritos are best used within 2 to 3 months. In the fridge, they keep 3 to 4 days.

recipes.title: Baked oatmeal squares
recipes.summary: A family-size breakfast that slices into grab-and-go squares.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease an 8-inch square pan.
Mix the oats, baking powder and cinnamon.
Whisk the milk, eggs and banana, then stir into the oats with the blueberries.
Pour into the pan and bake for 35 minutes, until set and golden.
Cool and cut into 9 squares. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.
tips: Ripe bananas sweeten it, so there's no need for added sugar.

recipes.title: Hummus veggie wrap
recipes.summary: Roll it up in five minutes and eat with one hand.
steps: Spread the hummus over the tortilla.
Add the vegetables in a line down the middle.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.
tips: Hummus is made with tahini (sesame).

recipes.title: Chicken and quinoa salad
recipes.summary: Four lunches made at once, ready to grab from the fridge.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken breast (cooked to 165°F), chopped
2 cups chopped cucumber and cherry tomatoes
steps: Cook the quinoa according to the package and let it cool.
Divide the quinoa among 4 containers.
Add the chickpeas, vegetables and chicken. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and pepper and keep it in a small separate pot or jar.
Seal and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days (salads like this don't freeze well). Pour on the dressing just before eating.
tips: Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.

recipes.title: White bean and tuna salad
recipes.summary: A no-cook, protein-packed lunch in ten minutes.
steps: Mix the tuna, beans, onion and tomatoes in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil, lemon juice and pepper.
Stir through the parsley. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days; tuna salad doesn't freeze well.
tips: Canned light tuna is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list for lower mercury. While breastfeeding, the FDA advises 2 to 3 servings (4 oz each) a week from that list.
Canned white (albacore) tuna is a "Good Choice" instead; the FDA advises no more than 1 serving a week of fish from that list.

recipes.title: Black bean and corn quesadillas
recipes.summary: A super-fast weeknight lifesaver: crispy, cheesy and ready in about 10 minutes.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
1 tbsp butter or oil for the pan
steps: Mix the beans, corn and salsa in a bowl.
Sprinkle cheese over half of each tortilla, add a scoop of the bean mixture, top with a little more cheese, and fold over.
Melt a little butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the quesadillas for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese is melted.
Cut into triangles and serve with sour cream or guacamole.
tips: Sharing with a baby or toddler? Whole corn kernels are a choking hazard; mash them with the beans or leave them out.

recipes.title: One-pot red lentil soup
recipes.summary: A big pot of warming soup that freezes beautifully.
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and broth. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Blend partly or fully if you like it smooth.
Cool, then refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze in portions and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.
tips: Use low-sodium or no-salt-added broth and tomatoes, and blend a plain portion if you're sharing with your baby.

recipes.title: One-pot turkey chili
recipes.summary: A mild, family-friendly chili for batch cooking.
steps: Brown the turkey in the oil, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spices, beans and tomatoes. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve with rice. Refrigerate leftovers for 3 to 4 days, or freeze portions and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.
tips: Halal depends on the turkey you buy; check the label.
Sharing with a baby or toddler? Mash the beans (whole beans are a choking hazard) and choose low-sodium or no-salt-added canned beans and tomatoes.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan lemon garlic salmon and broccoli
recipes.summary: Salmon, broccoli and peppers roasted on one pan with lemon and garlic. Zero messy pots.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Put the salmon and vegetables on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with oil and season with the garlic, salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Lay the lemon slices on top of the salmon.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork (145°F) and the broccoli is tender with crispy edges.
tips: Salmon is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list. While breastfeeding, the FDA advises 2 to 3 servings (4 oz each) a week from that list.
Sharing with a baby or toddler? Remove the skin, check carefully for bones, and flake the fish into small pieces.
Refrigerate leftovers and eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.title: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry
recipes.summary: Fast, colorful and easy to adapt.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the chicken until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F. Set aside.
Stir-fry the vegetables for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce and chicken and toss for 1 minute.
Serve over rice.
tips: Most soy sauce contains wheat; tamari labeled gluten-free is an option.
Refrigerate leftovers and eat within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.title: One-pot tomato and spinach pasta
recipes.summary: Pasta and sauce cook together in one pot.
steps: Add the pasta, tomatoes, water, garlic and oil to a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring often, for 10 to 12 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the Parmesan.
tips: Some Parmesan isn't vegetarian, halal or kosher (it may contain animal rennet); check the label.

recipes.title: Coconut chickpea curry
recipes.summary: A gentle, creamy curry that freezes well.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder.
Add the chickpeas, coconut milk and tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Serve with rice.
tips: Sharing with a baby or toddler? Mash the chickpeas; whole beans are a choking hazard.
Refrigerate leftovers for 3 to 4 days, or freeze portions and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.

recipes.title: Slow-cooker shredded chicken
recipes.summary: Ten minutes in the morning, dinner ready by evening.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless chicken breasts or thighs
steps: Put the chicken in the slow cooker and sprinkle with the spices.
Pour in the broth, cover and cook on low for 4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Shred with two forks. Use in wraps, rice bowls or salads. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze portions and use within 2 to 6 months for best quality.
tips: Halal depends on the chicken you buy; check the label.
For a baby or toddler, shred the chicken finely; tough or large chunks of meat are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: No-bake oat energy bites
recipes.summary: Grab-and-go bites, sweetened with dates.
steps: Mix everything in a bowl until it holds together (add a splash of water if dry).
Roll into 16 balls.
Refrigerate for up to a week, or freeze.
tips: Not for babies or young children: whole bites and chunks of nut butter are choking hazards.

recipes.title: Apple slices with peanut butter
recipes.summary: The fastest snack with some staying power.
steps: Core and slice the apple.
Dip or spread with peanut butter.
tips: Not for babies or young children as is: raw apple pieces and thick peanut butter are choking hazards.

recipes.title: Cheese, crackers and fruit plate
recipes.summary: A no-cook mini meal you can graze on.
steps: Arrange everything on a plate or in a container with sections.
tips: Sharing with a toddler? Cut grapes into small pieces, slice cheese thinly instead of serving chunks, swap raw carrots for cooked soft ones, and skip crackers with seeds or whole grain kernels.

recipes.title: Classic tropical green
recipes.summary: A bright, fruity green smoothie with spinach, mango and pineapple.
steps: Add the coconut water and spinach to the blender first.
Blend on high for about 20 seconds, until the greens are completely liquefied.
Add the banana, mango and pineapple.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until completely smooth.
tips: Blending the greens with the liquid first gets rid of leafy bits.

recipes.title: Creamy avocado green
recipes.summary: Creamy and thick, with avocado, greens and chia to keep you full.
steps: Pour the almond milk into the blender, then add the greens, cucumber and apple.
Blend briefly to break down the greens and apple skin.
Add the avocado and chia seeds.
Blend on high for about 1 minute, until creamy and thick.
tips: Use any unsweetened milk you like, such as dairy, soy or oat, if you avoid nuts.

recipes.title: Cucumber ginger green
recipes.summary: A light, refreshing green smoothie with lemon, cucumber and fresh ginger.
ingredients: 1 cup cold water or coconut water
steps: Pour the water and lemon juice into the blender.
Add the ginger, cucumber, apple and kale.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until fully smooth.
tips: For a smoother, juice-like drink, pour it through a fine mesh strainer.

recipes.title: Matcha green tea smoothie
recipes.summary: A bright green, gently energizing smoothie with matcha, banana and hemp seeds.
ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened soy or oat milk
steps: Add the milk, matcha and hemp seeds first so the matcha dissolves evenly.
Add the spinach and banana.
Blend on medium-high for about 45 seconds, until smooth and bright green.
tips: Matcha contains caffeine. If you're breastfeeding, count it toward your daily caffeine, and ask your provider if you're unsure how much is right for you.

recipes.title: Triple berry
recipes.summary: Sweet-tart strawberries, blueberries and raspberries, blended until smooth.
steps: Add the almond milk to the blender first.
Add the berries, fresh or frozen, and the banana.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until smooth.
tips: Use any unsweetened milk you like, such as dairy, soy or oat, if you avoid nuts.

recipes.title: Wild blueberry flax
recipes.summary: Thick and velvety, with wild blueberries, Greek yogurt, flaxseed and cinnamon.
steps: Add the almond milk and yogurt to the blender.
Add the flaxseed, cinnamon and blueberries.
Blend on high for 50 to 60 seconds, until velvety and thick.
tips: Use any unsweetened milk you like, such as dairy, soy or oat, if you avoid nuts.

recipes.title: Pomegranate acai
recipes.summary: A deep purple smoothie with acai, pomegranate juice and strawberries.
steps: Run warm water over the acai packet for about 5 seconds, then break it into chunks.
Pour the pomegranate juice and water into the blender.
Add the chia seeds, strawberries and acai.
Blend on high for about 1 minute.
tips: Choose pasteurized juice.

recipes.title: Peanut butter banana protein shake
recipes.summary: Thick and creamy, with peanut butter, banana and protein powder.
ingredients: 1 scoop vanilla protein powder (whey or plant-based)
steps: Pour the almond milk into the blender, then add the protein powder and peanut butter, so the powder doesn't stick.
Add the banana.
Blend on high for about 45 seconds, until thick and creamy.
tips: Check the protein powder label: many contain milk or soy. Supplements aren't reviewed by the FDA before they're sold, so look for one tested by an independent lab, and ask your provider if you're breastfeeding.

recipes.title: Chocolate hemp seed shake
recipes.summary: A chocolatey plant-based shake with hemp seeds, cacao and banana.
steps: Add the oat milk, cacao powder, vanilla and hemp seeds to the blender.
Add the banana on top.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until the hemp seeds are finely blended and the shake is smooth.
tips: Cacao contains a little caffeine.

recipes.title: Greek yogurt berry
recipes.summary: Rich and smooth, with Greek yogurt and mixed berries.
ingredients: 1/2 cup water or milk of your choice
steps: Add the water or milk, sweetener and yogurt to the blender.
Add the berries.
Pulse 3 or 4 times to crush the berries, then blend on high for about 45 seconds, until smooth.
tips: Never give honey to a baby under 12 months, even a taste.

recipes.title: Salted caramel date shake
recipes.summary: A sweet treat with dates, banana and a pinch of sea salt.
ingredients: 1 scoop vanilla protein powder (whey or plant-based)
steps: Chop or tear the dates into small pieces.
Pour the almond milk into the blender, then add the dates, protein powder and salt.
Add the banana.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until the dates are fully blended into a caramel-like shake.
tips: Check the protein powder label: many contain milk or soy.

recipes.title: Citrus sunshine
recipes.summary: A sunny orange smoothie with orange, mango, carrot and turmeric.
steps: Add the liquid, orange, carrot and turmeric to the blender.
Blend on high for about 30 seconds to break down the carrot.
Add the chia seeds and mango.
Blend on high for another 45 seconds.
tips: Fresh turmeric can stain, so rinse the blender right away.

recipes.title: Ginger turmeric pineapple
recipes.summary: Bright yellow and silky, with pineapple, banana, ginger and turmeric.
steps: Add the coconut water, ginger, turmeric and black pepper to the blender.
Add the pineapple and banana.
Blend on high for about 45 seconds, until bright yellow and silky.
tips: Black pepper is a classic partner for turmeric.

recipes.title: Golden milk tropical
recipes.summary: Rich and creamy, with mango, turmeric, cinnamon and kefir.
steps: Add the coconut milk, kefir or yogurt, turmeric and cinnamon to the blender.
Add the mango and banana.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until rich and smooth.
tips: Use a coconut yogurt for a dairy-free version.

recipes.title: Papaya mint
recipes.summary: Light and refreshing, with papaya, fresh mint and lemon.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen papaya chunks
steps: Pour the coconut water and lemon juice into the blender.
Add the mint, chia seeds and papaya.
Blend on high for about 45 seconds, until smooth.

recipes.title: Pear cinnamon oat
recipes.summary: Thick and cozy, with pear, oats and cinnamon.
steps: Add the oat milk, oats and cinnamon first so the oats can soak up a little liquid.
Add the pear and banana.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until velvety.
tips: Use certified gluten-free oats if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Kiwi lime green
recipes.summary: Zingy and green, with kiwi, cucumber, spinach and lime.
steps: Add the water, lime juice, spinach and cucumber to the blender.
Blend on high for about 20 seconds.
Add the kiwis and blend on medium-high for another 30 seconds, so the seeds don't get crushed and turn bitter.

recipes.title: Blueberry oatmeal breakfast
recipes.summary: A thick, filling breakfast in a cup, with oats, blueberries and almond butter.
steps: Pulse the oats in the blender 5 times to break them into a coarse flour.
Add the almond milk, almond butter, banana and blueberries.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until thick.
tips: Use certified gluten-free oats if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Creamy almond fig
recipes.summary: Naturally sweet and creamy, with figs, almond butter and flaxseed.
ingredients: 3 dried or fresh figs, stems removed
steps: If using dried figs, soak them in warm water for 5 minutes to soften.
Add the soy milk, almond butter, flaxseed and figs to the blender.
Add the banana.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds, until smooth.

recipes.title: Tahini date
recipes.summary: Rich and nutty, with tahini, dates and banana.
steps: Chop the dates into small pieces.
Add the oat milk, tahini, dates and hemp seeds to the blender.
Add the banana.
Blend on high for 60 to 90 seconds, until the dates are completely smooth.

recipes.title: Turkey taco skillet
recipes.summary: Taco night flavor in one pan, with turkey, black beans and corn.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Brown the turkey in a large skillet over medium-high heat until fully cooked, 6 to 7 minutes.
Stir in the taco seasoning and 1/4 cup water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes with their juices, and corn. Simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until heated through.
Sprinkle the cheese over the top, cover for 2 minutes until melted, and top with cilantro.
Serve with avocado or whole-wheat tortillas.
tips: Cook chicken and turkey to 165°F.
Check the taco seasoning label if you avoid gluten.
Sharing with a baby or toddler? Whole corn kernels are a choking hazard; mash them or leave them out.

recipes.title: Lemon herb chicken and asparagus
recipes.summary: Golden chicken and tender-crisp asparagus in a bright lemon-garlic pan sauce.
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, cut into cutlets or bite-size pieces
1 bunch thin asparagus, trimmed and cut into thirds
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper and oregano and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and the asparagus to the pan. Sauté for 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Pour in the lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the chicken, toss in the pan juices, and top with lemon zest.
tips: Cook chicken and turkey to 165°F.

recipes.title: Creamy spinach and tomato gnocchi
recipes.summary: Comfort food made fast: soft gnocchi in a creamy garlic, tomato and spinach sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup heavy cream or canned coconut milk
steps: Cook the gnocchi in boiling salted water as the package directs, usually 2 to 3 minutes, and drain when they float.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté the garlic and tomatoes for 3 minutes, until the tomatoes start to burst.
Stir in the cream and spinach until the spinach wilts, about 1 minute.
Add the gnocchi and parmesan and stir until coated in a creamy sauce.
tips: Most gnocchi contain wheat; check the label.
For dairy-free, use olive oil and coconut milk and skip the parmesan.

recipes.title: Ground beef and broccoli stir-fry
recipes.summary: Better than takeout: savory ground beef and broccoli in a glossy ginger-soy sauce.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
steps: Brown the beef in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until cooked through. Drain extra fat if needed.
Add the garlic, ginger, broccoli and 2 tbsp water. Cover for 3 minutes to steam the broccoli until bright green and tender-crisp.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey and cornstarch mixture, pour it in, and stir for 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve over rice or cauliflower rice.
tips: Cook ground beef to 160°F.
Use tamari labeled gluten-free if you avoid wheat.
Sharing with a baby? Never give honey to a baby under 12 months.

recipes.title: Creamy tomato tortellini soup
recipes.summary: A cozy, creamy tomato soup with cheese tortellini and spinach that kids tend to love.
ingredients: 3 cups low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth
1 can (28 oz) crushed or diced tomatoes
1/2 cup heavy cream or cream cheese
steps: In a medium pot, combine the broth, tomatoes, garlic, Italian seasoning and a pinch of salt and pepper. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Add the tortellini and cook as the package directs, about 4 to 5 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cream and spinach until the spinach wilts.
Ladle into bowls and top with parmesan.
tips: Use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian.

recipes.title: Black bean and sweet potato chili
recipes.summary: A cozy plant-based chili with black beans, sweet potato and warm spices.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced small
2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: In a medium pot, cook the onion and sweet potato in the oil for 5 minutes, until the onion is translucent. Dicing the sweet potato small helps it cook quickly.
Add the chili powder and cumin and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sweet potato is fork-tender.
tips: Freeze leftovers in portions for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Coconut curry chickpea soup
recipes.summary: A fragrant, creamy chickpea soup with coconut milk, curry and spinach.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
steps: Heat the oil in a soup pot over medium heat. Sauté the onion, garlic and ginger for 3 to 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, coconut milk and broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach just before serving, until wilted.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan sausage and pepper hash
recipes.summary: A hearty, low-prep dinner of crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan.
ingredients: 4 chicken or turkey sausage links, sliced into rounds
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil, salt and pepper on a baking sheet and roast for 10 minutes.
Add the sausage, peppers and onion. Drizzle with the rest of the oil and sprinkle with paprika.
Toss and roast for another 15 minutes, until the potatoes are crispy and the sausage is browned.
tips: Cook chicken or turkey sausage to 165°F, unless the package says it's fully cooked.
Check sausage labels for allergens and gluten.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan honey mustard chicken
recipes.summary: Sweet and savory chicken tenders and green beans, all on one pan.
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, cut into bite-size tenders
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Whisk the mustard, honey, oil and garlic powder in a small bowl.
Put the chicken and green beans on a baking sheet, pour over the sauce and toss to coat.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the beans are tender-crisp.
tips: Cook chicken and turkey to 165°F.
Sharing with a baby? Never give honey to a baby under 12 months.

recipes.title: Mediterranean tuna pita pockets
recipes.summary: No-cook tuna salad with yogurt, cucumber, tomato and feta, stuffed into pitas.
ingredients: 2 cans (5 oz each) light tuna in water, drained
steps: Flake the tuna in a medium bowl with a fork.
Stir in the yogurt, olive oil, salt and pepper until creamy.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes and feta.
Store the tuna salad in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Spoon into warmed pita pockets just before eating.
tips: Canned light tuna is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list. Albacore (white) tuna is a "Good Choice": have no more than 1 serving a week.

recipes.title: Teriyaki chicken rice bowls
recipes.summary: Chicken, vegetables and brown rice in a glossy teriyaki sauce.
ingredients: 2 cups precooked or microwave brown rice
2 cups mixed stir-fry vegetables, such as snap peas, carrots and broccoli
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Add the vegetables and 2 tbsp water. Cover for 3 minutes to steam.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce and simmer for 2 minutes, until glossy and thick.
Serve over warm brown rice.
tips: Cook chicken and turkey to 165°F.
Most teriyaki sauce contains soy and wheat; check the label.

recipes.title: Garlic butter shrimp pasta
recipes.summary: Feel fancy with minimal effort: shrimp and pasta in a lemony garlic butter sauce.
ingredients: 1/4 cup chicken broth or pasta water
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water as the package directs. Save 1/4 cup pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and shrimp and cook for about 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Set the shrimp aside.
Add the broth and lemon juice to the pan, scraping up the browned bits.
Toss in the pasta, shrimp and reserved pasta water until coated. Top with parsley.
tips: Shrimp is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list.

recipes.title: Creamy mushroom pasta
recipes.summary: Vegetarian comfort in a flash: golden mushrooms in a creamy parmesan sauce.
ingredients: 8 oz button or cremini mushrooms, sliced
1/2 cup heavy cream or cream cheese
steps: Cook the pasta as the package directs and drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden and their liquid has evaporated.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cream and parmesan and simmer for 2 minutes, until creamy.
Toss in the pasta until well coated.

recipes.title: Pesto chicken and tomato penne
recipes.summary: A pantry-shortcut dinner with jarred pesto, rotisserie chicken and cherry tomatoes.
ingredients: 2 cooked chicken breasts, shredded or diced (rotisserie chicken works great)
steps: Cook the penne as the package directs. Save 2 tbsp pasta water, then drain.
Off the heat, toss the pasta in the warm pot with the chicken, pesto, tomatoes and reserved pasta water.
Sprinkle with parmesan and serve right away.
tips: Many pestos contain pine nuts, other nuts and cheese; check the label.

recipes.title: Spinach, tomato and feta frittata
recipes.summary: A protein-packed, low-prep frittata with spinach, tomatoes and feta.
steps: Heat the oven broiler to high.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the tomatoes and spinach for 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Pour in the eggs and sprinkle with feta. Cook without stirring for 5 minutes, until the edges set.
Broil for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden, puffed and set in the middle.
tips: Cook until the center is firm, with no runny egg.

recipes.title: Huevos rancheros bowls
recipes.summary: Bold flavors from pantry staples: eggs, black beans, salsa and avocado on warm tortillas.
steps: Warm the beans in a small pot.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet.
In the same skillet, fry the eggs in a little oil.
Put a tortilla in each bowl and top with beans, salsa, avocado and a fried egg.
tips: Sharing with a baby or toddler? Cook their egg until the white and yolk are firm.

recipes.title: Naan margherita pizzas
recipes.summary: Friday-night pizza made fast on store-bought naan.
ingredients: 4 pieces store-bought naan, garlic or plain
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Lay the naan on a baking sheet and spread each with a few tablespoons of sauce.
Top with mozzarella and tomatoes.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Top with basil and slice.
tips: Many naans contain milk and egg; check the label.

recipes.title: BBQ chicken flatbread
recipes.summary: Sweet, savory and effortless, with rotisserie chicken, red onion and melty cheese.
ingredients: 2 large flatbreads or premade pizza crusts
1 cup shredded cooked chicken (rotisserie chicken works great)
1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella and gouda cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken with half the BBQ sauce.
Spread the rest of the sauce over the flatbreads and top with the cheese, chicken and onion.
Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, until the crust is crisp and the cheese is bubbly. Top with cilantro.
tips: Check BBQ sauce labels: some contain fish (in Worcestershire sauce) or honey.

recipes.title: Strawberry banana oat smoothie
recipes.summary: Oats, flax and fruit blended thick and creamy.
steps: Add the milk, oats, brewer's yeast and flaxseed to the blender first.
Add the strawberries, banana, vanilla and honey.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds until completely smooth.
tips: Honey is fine for you, but never give honey to a baby under 12 months.
Use oat or soy milk to make it dairy-free.

recipes.title: Almond butter power shake
recipes.summary: Almond butter, chia and oats for a filling, frothy shake.
steps: Pour the almond milk and water into the blender.
Add the oats, chia seeds and almond butter, then the banana and ice.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds until smooth and frothy.
tips: For gluten-free, choose oats labeled gluten-free.

recipes.title: Mango avocado smoothie
recipes.summary: Mango and avocado blended silky smooth, with spinach if you like.
ingredients: 1 cup coconut water or oat milk
1 cup fresh baby spinach (optional; it turns the smoothie green)
steps: Pour the coconut water or oat milk into the blender, add the spinach and blend until smooth.
Add the mango and avocado.
Blend on high for about 45 seconds until silky.

recipes.title: Chocolate peanut butter shake
recipes.summary: Rich and milkshake-like, made with oat milk and a frozen banana.
steps: Add the oat milk, peanut butter, cacao powder, brewer's yeast and oats to the blender.
Add the frozen banana.
Blend on high for about 60 seconds until thick and creamy.
tips: Cocoa contains a small amount of caffeine; leave it out if you're keeping caffeine low.

recipes.title: Chocolate chip oat bites
recipes.summary: No-bake bites to keep in the fridge for one-handed snacking.
ingredients: 1/2 cup natural peanut butter or almond butter
steps: In a medium bowl, mix the nut butter, honey and vanilla well.
Stir in the oats, flaxseed and brewer's yeast until a dough forms.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Roll into 1-inch balls and keep in the fridge for up to a week.
tips: Honey is fine for you, but never give honey to a baby under 12 months.
Not for babies or young children: whole bites and chunks of nut butter are choking hazards.

recipes.title: No-bake oat granola bars
recipes.summary: Press, chill and slice. Snack bars ready for the week.
steps: Line an 8x8-inch pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix the almond butter and maple syrup until smooth.
Stir in the oats, flaxseed and chia seeds.
Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the pan, then press the chocolate chips into the top.
Freeze for 30 minutes, then slice into bars.
tips: Keep the bars in the fridge for up to a week, or freeze them.
Not for babies or young children: chunky bars are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: Oatmeal chocolate chip cookies
recipes.summary: A big batch of classic chewy oat cookies with flax and brewer's yeast.
ingredients: 2 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 2 tbsp water (let sit 3 minutes)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then beat in the eggs and the flaxseed mixture.
In another bowl, whisk the flour, brewer's yeast and baking soda, then mix it into the butter mixture.
Stir in the oats and chocolate chips.
Scoop rounded tablespoons onto a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden.
tips: Don't eat the raw dough: it contains raw eggs and raw flour.
Freeze the extra cookies and take out a few at a time.

recipes.title: Brown sugar oats with banana
recipes.summary: Warm, creamy oats cooked in oat milk with a caramel-like finish.
ingredients: 1 tbsp brown sugar or coconut sugar
steps: Bring the oat milk to a gentle simmer in a small pot.
Stir in the oats and turn the heat down to medium-low.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy.
Stir in the sugar and flaxseed, then top with banana and cacao nibs.

recipes.title: Blueberry flax yogurt bowl
recipes.summary: Greek yogurt, blueberries and flax with a drizzle of honey.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh or dried wild blueberries
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Sprinkle the flaxseed on one side and pile the blueberries on the other.
Drizzle with honey and eat right away.
tips: Honey is fine for you, but never give honey to a baby under 12 months.

recipes.title: Overnight oat milk chia pudding
recipes.summary: Stir it tonight and wake up to a thick, creamy pudding.
steps: In a jar, whisk the oat milk, chia seeds, vanilla and maple syrup.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight, until thick.
Top with raspberries before serving.
tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
For gluten-free, choose an oat milk labeled gluten-free.

recipes.title: Avocado toast with brewer's yeast
recipes.summary: Crisp sourdough, thick smashed avocado and a savory sprinkle.
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with salt and pepper and spread it thickly on the toast.
Dust lightly with brewer's yeast and finish with red pepper flakes.

recipes.title: Sweet potato coconut stew
recipes.summary: A warm, gently spiced one-pot stew with spinach.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in a little oil in a large pot.
Add the sweet potatoes, broth and coconut milk.
Simmer for about 15 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and serve warm.
tips: Sharing with a baby? Mash some sweet potato with a little of the broth.
Refrigerate leftovers for 3 to 4 days, or freeze portions.

recipes.title: Moroccan barley milk soup (hssoua)
recipes.summary: A traditional warm, creamy barley soup scented with anise.
steps: Rinse the barley well.
In a pot, combine the barley, water, anise seeds and olive oil.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 20 minutes until the barley is soft.
Stir in the milk and simmer gently for 5 more minutes. Season and serve warm.
tips: Barley contains gluten.
Use oat or soy milk to make it dairy-free.

recipes.title: Chicken and vegetable bone broth soup
recipes.summary: A simple, warming broth soup with carrots, ginger and chicken.
ingredients: 4 cups chicken or beef bone broth
steps: Add the broth, onion, carrots, celery and ginger to a pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Add the chicken, heat through, and season lightly.
tips: Store-bought broth can be salty; choose a low-sodium one if sharing with little ones.
Reheat leftovers until steaming hot. Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days.

recipes.title: Salmon, arugula and quinoa bowl
recipes.summary: Baked salmon on quinoa and peppery greens with lemon.
steps: Bake the salmon at 400°F (200°C) for about 12 minutes, until it reaches 145°F.
Layer the quinoa and arugula in a bowl.
Top with the salmon and avocado, then drizzle with olive oil and lemon.
tips: Salmon is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list. While breastfeeding, the FDA advises 2 to 3 servings (4 oz each) a week from that list.

recipes.title: Chicken curry with fenugreek leaves (methi murgh)
recipes.summary: A fragrant home-style curry with fresh or dried methi leaves.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh fenugreek (methi) leaves, chopped, or 2 tbsp dried
steps: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in oil until golden.
Add the turmeric and cumin, then the blended tomatoes, and cook until the oil separates.
Add the chicken and fenugreek leaves, cover and simmer for about 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
tips: Fenugreek is in the same plant family as peanuts and chickpeas. If you're allergic to either, check with your doctor first.
Sharing with a baby or toddler? Shred the chicken finely.

recipes.title: Spinach, pear and quinoa salad
recipes.summary: Sweet pear, crunchy seeds and greens with balsamic dressing.
steps: Toss the spinach and quinoa in a large bowl.
Top with the pear, pistachios and cranberries.
Drizzle lightly with vinaigrette before serving.
tips: Use pumpkin seeds instead of pistachios to keep it nut-free.

recipes.title: Peanut butter banana baked oatmeal cups
recipes.summary: Grab-and-go oatmeal cups to bake once and eat all week.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
In a large bowl, whisk the milk, peanut butter, maple syrup, eggs, mashed banana and cinnamon.
Stir in the oats and flaxseed.
Divide among the muffin cups and top each with a banana slice.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until set and golden.
tips: Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze and warm one in the microwave.
Use oat or soy milk to make them dairy-free.

recipes.title: Almond butter chia pudding
recipes.summary: Creamy, nutty chia pudding that sets overnight in the fridge.
ingredients: 1 cup oat milk or almond milk
Sliced almonds or fresh berries for topping
steps: In a jar or bowl, whisk the milk, almond butter, maple syrup and vanilla until mostly smooth.
Stir in the chia seeds.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Stir well and top with sliced almonds or berries.
tips: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
For gluten-free, choose an oat milk labeled gluten-free.

recipes.title: Sweet potato and spinach breakfast hash
recipes.summary: A one-pan hash with tender sweet potato, greens and eggs.
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced small
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the sweet potato and onion, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender and lightly browned.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make two small wells, crack an egg into each, cover, and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are firm, about 4 to 5 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
tips: The FDA advises cooking eggs until both the yolk and white are firm.
Sharing with a baby? Mash some sweet potato and finely chop a little of the firm egg.

recipes.title: Warm apple cinnamon porridge
recipes.summary: Soft cooked apples and cinnamon stirred into creamy oats.
steps: Melt the butter in a small pot over medium heat, add the apple and cinnamon, and cook for about 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the oat milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the oats and brewer's yeast and turn the heat to medium-low.
Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Top with the walnuts.
tips: Use coconut oil instead of butter to make it dairy-free.
Sharing with a baby? Leave off the walnuts; whole and chopped nuts are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: Lemon herb quinoa and chickpea salad
recipes.summary: High in protein and fiber, and it stays fresh for days without getting soggy.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Add the quinoa, chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber and feta and toss well.
Divide into containers and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
tips: Leave out the feta to make it dairy-free.
Sharing with a baby or toddler? Quarter the tomatoes and mash the chickpeas; whole ones are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: Greek chicken salad jars
recipes.summary: Layered so the greens stay crisp until you shake it into a bowl.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked shredded chicken (rotisserie works great)
2 cups baby spinach or mixed greens
3 tbsp tzatziki or Greek yogurt dressing
steps: Spoon the dressing into the bottom of 2 mason jars or airtight containers.
Layer the cucumber, olives and peppers next.
Add the chicken, then pack the greens tightly on top.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days. To eat, tip into a bowl and toss.
tips: Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.
Store rotisserie chicken in the fridge within 2 hours of buying it and use within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.title: Creamy chicken salad lettuce wraps
recipes.summary: A light, crunchy chicken salad you scoop into crisp lettuce leaves.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken breast, diced or shredded
Large crisp lettuce leaves (romaine or butter lettuce)
steps: In a bowl, mix the chicken, yogurt, mustard, cranberries and nuts.
Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 4 days.
Scoop into lettuce leaves when ready to eat.
tips: Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.
Leave out the nuts to make it nut-free, and when sharing with little ones; nuts are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: High-protein bento box
recipes.summary: No cooking, just packing: turkey, eggs, hummus, veggies and crunch.
ingredients: A handful of crackers or whole-grain pita slices
steps: Roll up the turkey slices and put them in one section of a divided container.
Add the halved eggs and crackers to another, the carrots and hummus to the center, and the nuts to the last.
Seal and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
tips: Opened deli meat keeps 3 to 5 days in the fridge; check the date on the pack.
Whole nuts and baby carrots are choking hazards for babies and young children.

recipes.title: Cold soba noodles with peanut sauce and edamame
recipes.summary: Plant-based protein and cold noodles that taste even better the next day.
steps: Cook the soba noodles according to the package, then rinse under cold water. Steam the edamame.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, maple syrup and warm water into a sauce.
Toss the noodles, edamame and carrot in the sauce.
Divide into containers and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
tips: Most soba noodles contain wheat as well as buckwheat. For wheat-free, look for 100% buckwheat soba and gluten-free tamari.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan chicken fajita bowls
recipes.summary: Spiced chicken and peppers roasted on one pan, over rice or quinoa.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked brown rice or quinoa
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil and seasoning on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Divide the rice and fajita mix among 4 containers. Refrigerate for up to 4 days and eat cold or reheated until steaming.
tips: Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.
Some seasoning mixes contain wheat; check the label if you need gluten-free.

recipes.title: Pesto chicken and veggie pasta salad
recipes.summary: A cold pasta salad that packs well and keeps you full.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken, shredded or diced
steps: Cook the pasta according to the package, drain and rinse under cold water.
In a large bowl, toss the cooled pasta with the pesto, chicken, tomatoes, spinach and parmesan.
Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
tips: Many pestos contain pine nuts, other nuts and cheese; check the label.
Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.

recipes.title: Sweet potato and black bean quinoa bowls
recipes.summary: Fiber-rich vegetarian bowls that hold up all week.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, peeled and diced
1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the sweet potato with the oil and cumin and roast for about 20 minutes, until tender.
Divide the quinoa among containers, then top with the sweet potato, beans and corn.
Drizzle with lime juice, seal and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
tips: Sharing with a baby or toddler? Mash the beans and sweet potato; whole beans and corn kernels are a choking hazard.

recipes.title: Turkey meatball and zucchini noodle box
recipes.summary: Comfort food that reheats in two minutes.
ingredients: 3 medium zucchini, spiralized, or 2 cups cooked whole-wheat spaghetti
steps: Divide the zucchini noodles or spaghetti among 4 containers.
Top each with 3 meatballs and a scoop of marinara, then sprinkle with parmesan.
Seal and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Microwave about 2 minutes, until steaming hot (165°F), before eating.
tips: Pre-made meatballs often contain egg, wheat and milk; check the label.
Zucchini noodles release water as they sit; keep them in a separate container if you prefer them firmer.

recipes.title: Golden spinach and egg scramble
recipes.summary: One pan of eggs and spinach: with feta on sourdough toast for you, as soft egg strips with avocado or a smooth mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: scrambled eggs cooked in olive oil with baby spinach, crumbled feta and black pepper, served on sourdough toast. Take baby’s portion out before adding feta and salt.

ingredients: Breast milk or formula, to thin the mash
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pan and wilt the spinach.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently until fully set, with no runny parts.
Set aside baby’s portion before adding feta, salt or pepper.
For finger food: cut baby’s egg into soft, wide strips and serve with thick avocado spears.
For a mash: mash cooked egg yolk with ripe avocado, thinned with a little breast milk or formula.
Finish the grown-up eggs with feta and black pepper and serve on sourdough toast.
tips: Egg is a common allergen. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Finger-squish test: many parents check that any vegetable or protein served as finger food squishes easily between their thumb and index finger.

recipes.title: Cinnamon berry and chia oatmeal
recipes.summary: One pot of cinnamon oats: with walnuts and maple for you, with mashed blueberries for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: warm rolled oats cooked in milk with cinnamon and chia seeds, finished with a drizzle of maple syrup, toasted walnuts and fresh blueberries. Cook baby’s oats in water, breast milk or formula, and keep maple syrup and honey for the grown-ups.

ingredients: Breast milk or formula, to thin baby’s portion
steps: Simmer the oats in the water with the cinnamon for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the chia seeds and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Spoon out baby’s portion and thin it with a little breast milk or formula until smooth and spoonable.
Mash the blueberries well (or stew the apple until soft) and swirl them through baby’s oats.
Finish the grown-up bowls with milk, maple, walnuts and whole blueberries.
tips: Mash blueberries well for babies: whole blueberries are a choking risk.
Keep honey out of baby’s bowl until after the first birthday.

recipes.title: Fluffy banana and ricotta pancakes
recipes.summary: One batter of banana and ricotta pancakes: with berries and almonds for you, as strips or soft soaked bits for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: stack of whole wheat banana ricotta pancakes topped with maple syrup, fresh berries and toasted sliced almonds.

ingredients: A little oil for the pan
steps: Whisk the mashed banana, ricotta and eggs, then fold in the flour and baking powder.
Cook small pancakes in a lightly oiled pan for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until cooked through.
For finger food: cut baby’s pancake into strips about the size of an adult finger, easy for a palmar grasp.
For a mash: tear a pancake into small soft bits and soak them in a little warm breast milk or formula.
Top the grown-up stack with maple, berries and toasted almonds.
tips: Egg, dairy and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Pancakes freeze well: cool, stack with parchment and reheat in the toaster.

recipes.title: Mediterranean salmon, sweet potato and broccoli
recipes.summary: One tray of salmon, sweet potato and broccoli: with garlic-lemon broccoli for you, as soft wedges or a flaked salmon mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: flaky oven-roasted salmon with roasted sweet potato wedges and garlic-lemon sautéed broccoli. Set baby’s portion aside before you season.

ingredients: 2 to 3 skinless salmon fillets (one for baby)
steps: Cut the sweet potatoes into long, thick wedges.
Roast the wedges at 400°F for 15 minutes, then add the salmon and bake 12 to 15 minutes more, until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F.
Steam a few large broccoli florets with a thick stalk to hold until very soft. Sauté the rest with garlic and lemon for the grown-ups.
For finger food: peel baby’s sweet potato wedges and serve them with the soft broccoli florets.
For a mash: check baby’s salmon carefully for small bones, flake it and mash it with sweet potato and a drop of olive oil.
Season the grown-up plates with salt and pepper at the table.
tips: Always double-check flaked fish for small bones.
Fish is a common allergen. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.

recipes.title: Creamy avocado and cannellini bean salad
recipes.summary: One bowl of white beans and avocado: a fresh salad with feta for you, as hemp-rolled wedges or a creamy mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: white beans tossed with ripe avocado, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, feta, olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.

ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) no-salt-added cannellini beans, rinsed
A squeeze of fresh orange or lemon juice
steps: Set aside about 1/2 cup of beans and a quarter of an avocado for baby.
For finger food: cut ripe avocado into wedges, roll them in hemp seeds for grip and serve with lightly smushed beans.
For a mash: mash the beans and avocado together with a squeeze of orange or lemon juice.
Toss the rest with the tomatoes, cucumber, feta, olive oil, lemon, salt and pepper for the grown-ups.
tips: Flatten each bean between your fingers before serving: whole beans can be hard for new eaters to manage.
Halve or quarter cherry tomatoes for older kids; keep them off baby’s plate whole.

recipes.title: Golden lentil and carrot dahl
recipes.summary: One pot of coconut lentil dahl: with naan and cilantro for you, as a soft spoonable mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: red lentils stewed with coconut milk, carrots, ginger, turmeric, garlic and cumin, salted to taste and served with naan and cilantro. Scoop out baby’s portion before adding salt.

steps: Soften the garlic and ginger in the pot, then stir in the turmeric and cumin.
Add the lentils, carrots, coconut milk and water and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
Scoop out baby’s portion before adding salt and mash it until smooth.
Serve baby’s dahl warm as a spoonable mash or on a pre-loaded spoon.
Salt the rest to taste and serve with naan and cilantro.
tips: Lentils are a plant source of iron.
Scoop before seasoning: take baby’s portion out before adding salt, soy sauce, hot pepper or other spicy seasoning.

recipes.title: Gentle chicken and veggie noodle soup
recipes.summary: One pot of chicken noodle soup: with parsley, salt and pepper for you, as soft finger foods or a chunky blended soup for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: shredded chicken breast, carrots, celery and egg noodles simmered in rich chicken broth, finished with fresh parsley, salt and black pepper.

ingredients: 6 cups low-sodium or no-salt-added chicken broth
steps: Simmer the chicken, carrots and celery in the broth for about 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Cook the noodles in the soup until very soft.
Scoop out baby’s portion before adding salt or pepper.
For finger food: serve soft rotini, very soft carrot sticks and juicy shredded chicken.
For a mash: blend chicken, carrots, noodles and a little broth into a chunky soup.
Season the grown-up bowls with salt, pepper and parsley.
tips: Keep celery for the grown-ups or blend it well: its strings can be hard for babies.
Even low-sodium broth has some salt, so keep baby’s broth to a little for moistening.

recipes.title: Deconstructed turkey and lentil chili
recipes.summary: One pot of turkey and lentil chili: spiced and topped for you, mildly seasoned as crumbles or a fork mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: chunky chili of ground turkey, lentils, tomatoes and bell peppers, seasoned with chili powder and sea salt and topped with cheddar and cilantro. Take baby’s portion out before adding chili powder and salt.

steps: Brown the turkey in a large pot, breaking it up finely, until cooked through to 165°F.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, bell pepper, water, cumin and garlic powder. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are very soft.
Spoon out baby’s portion before adding any chili powder or salt.
For finger food: offer soft turkey crumbles and soft lentils for pincer-grasp practice.
For a mash: lightly mash turkey, lentils and stewed tomatoes with a fork.
Season the rest with chili powder and salt and top with cheddar and cilantro.
tips: Lentils and turkey are sources of iron.
Cool baby’s portion before serving, and freeze extra in small containers.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan roasted chicken, zucchini and squash
recipes.summary: One tray of chicken thighs and summer squash: herby and crisp-skinned for you, as soft spears and shredded chicken for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: skin-on chicken thighs, zucchini and yellow squash roasted with olive oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and sea salt. Season baby’s corner of the tray with olive oil and herbs only.

steps: Cut the zucchini and squash into long spears and toss with olive oil and herbs.
Keep baby’s chicken and spears on one corner of the tray, unsalted.
Roast at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are very soft.
For finger food: peel baby’s spears and serve with shredded tender thigh meat, skin removed.
For a mash: finely shred chicken thigh and mash it with soft roasted zucchini.
Season the grown-up portions with sea salt.
tips: Remove chicken skin and any bones before serving baby.
Finger-squish test: many parents check that any vegetable or protein served as finger food squishes easily between their thumb and index finger.

recipes.title: Slow-cooked beef and root vegetable stew
recipes.summary: One pot of slow-braised beef with carrots, potatoes and parsnips: seasoned at the table for you, shredded or mashed for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: tender chuck roast braised with carrots, potatoes, parsnips, rosemary and garlic in beef broth, seasoned to taste at the table.

ingredients: 3 cups low-sodium or no-salt-added beef broth
steps: Brown the beef in a heavy pot, then add the garlic, rosemary, vegetables and broth.
Cover and braise at 325°F (or on low in a slow cooker) for about 3 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
For finger food: shred baby’s beef very finely with a fork and serve with soft potato and carrot wedges.
For a mash: mash potato, carrot and shredded beef with a spoonful of warm broth.
Let the grown-ups season their bowls with salt and pepper at the table.
tips: Beef is a source of iron.
Remove the rosemary sprig before serving baby.

recipes.title: Creamy butternut squash and ricotta pasta
recipes.summary: One pot of squash and ricotta pasta: with parmesan and pepper for you, as sauce-coated rigatoni or a dipping puree for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: rigatoni or penne tossed in a sauce of pureed butternut squash, ricotta, nutmeg and garlic, finished with parmesan, salt and black pepper. Set baby’s portion aside before adding salt and parmesan.

steps: Steam or roast the squash with the garlic until very soft, then blend with the ricotta and nutmeg.
Cook the rigatoni until soft, a little past al dente for baby.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and set baby’s portion aside before adding salt or parmesan.
For finger food: serve large, well-cooked rigatoni coated in the sauce.
For a mash: mash the pasta slightly, or serve the sauce as a thick dip on a pre-loaded spoon.
Finish the grown-up bowls with parmesan, salt and black pepper.
tips: Dairy and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Large pasta shapes like rigatoni are easier for little hands than small ones.

recipes.title: Baked white fish with cauliflower and potato
recipes.summary: One bake of cod with cauliflower and potato: lemon butter and parmesan mash for you, as soft flakes and florets or a smooth mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: cod or halibut baked with lemon butter and fresh dill, over garlic-parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed cauliflower.

ingredients: 2 to 3 boneless cod or halibut fillets
Breast milk or formula, to thin
steps: Bake the fish at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F. Keep baby’s fillet plain.
Boil the potatoes and steam the cauliflower until very soft.
For finger food: flake baby’s fish, checking for bones, and serve with soft cauliflower florets.
For a mash: mash plain potato and cauliflower with flaked fish and a splash of breast milk, formula or olive oil.
Make the grown-up mash with garlic, parmesan, butter and salt, and finish the fish with lemon butter and dill.
tips: Always double-check flaked fish for small bones.
Fish is a common allergen. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.

recipes.title: Mild coconut chicken curry
recipes.summary: One pot of mild coconut curry: over brown rice for you, as sauce-coated chicken strips or a golden mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: chicken strips simmered in full-fat coconut milk with turmeric, ginger, garlic, sweet peas and bell peppers, over brown rice. Add chili and salt to the grown-up pot after baby’s portion is out.

ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into strips
1 red bell pepper, in long strips
steps: Roast the bell pepper strips at 400°F until very soft.
Soften the garlic and ginger, stir in the turmeric, then add the chicken and coconut milk and simmer until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes. Scoop out baby’s portion before adding salt or chili.
For finger food: serve soft chicken strips coated in sauce with the soft roasted pepper strips.
For a mash: blend chicken, peas and brown rice with a little sauce into a golden mash.
Season the rest and serve over brown rice.
tips: Mash or flatten peas for babies: whole peas can be a choking risk.
Scoop before seasoning: take baby’s portion out before adding salt, soy sauce, hot pepper or other spicy seasoning.

recipes.title: Italian beef and zucchini meatballs
recipes.summary: One batch of baked beef and zucchini meatballs: in marinara over spaghetti for you, as soft strips or a mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: baked beef and zucchini meatballs simmered in marinara and served over spaghetti. Mix a little salt into the grown-up batch only.

ingredients: 1 zucchini, finely grated and squeezed dry
steps: Mix the beef, zucchini, breadcrumbs, egg, garlic powder and oregano. Shape baby’s portion first, with no added salt.
Bake at 400°F for 18 to 20 minutes, until cooked through to 160°F.
For finger food: cut baby’s meatballs into strips or quarters. Never serve whole round meatballs to a young baby.
For a mash: mash a meatball with a little low-sodium tomato sauce or warm water.
Simmer the grown-up meatballs in marinara and serve over spaghetti.
tips: Egg and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Shape baby’s portion into small logs instead of balls for easier, safer grabbing.

recipes.title: Tofu, broccoli and sesame noodle bowl
recipes.summary: One bowl of tofu, broccoli and noodles: in a sesame-peanut sauce with chili for you, as soft strips or a mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: pan-seared tofu cubes, steamed broccoli and noodles tossed in a sesame-peanut sauce with soy sauce, lime and chili flakes. Add soy sauce and chili to the grown-up portion only.

steps: Bake plain tofu strips at 400°F for 20 minutes, until set but soft. Steam the broccoli until very soft and cook the noodles until soft.
Thin the peanut butter and tahini with warm water into a smooth, runny sauce.
For finger food: serve long strips of soft tofu, broccoli florets and soft noodles coated in a little of the thinned sauce.
For a mash: mash soft tofu and broccoli heads with a drop of warm water or thinned peanut butter.
Toss the grown-up bowls with the rest of the sauce, soy sauce, lime and chili flakes.
tips: Peanut, sesame, soy and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Always thin nut and seed butters: a thick spoonful is a choking risk.
